documents.title: Visiting Artist Welcome and Safeguarding Notes
Loan Instrument Repair and Recall Checklist
Quiet Room Operation and Emergency Notes

cases.query: How far ahead must our host request a workshop led by a visiting artist?

evidence.text: The guest office requires a visiting artist booking request at least 18 calendar days before the first workshop.

cases.query: Can our host move a confirmed guest class without a fee, and how much notice is needed?

evidence.text: A confirmed guest workshop may be moved once without an administration fee if the host gives seven full days of notice.

cases.query: The visiting choreographer cancelled. What choices does the office give participants and when is a refund due?

evidence.text: When a visiting artist cancels, the office offers either a replacement workshop or a full workshop-fee refund within ten business days.

cases.query: How early should a visiting teacher arrive for their first teaching session?

evidence.text: Visiting artists must check in 25 minutes before their first scheduled teaching session.

cases.query: Can an artist message a child directly to arrange private follow-up lessons?

evidence.text: A visiting artist must not arrange private follow-up coaching with a minor through the minor's personal messaging account.

cases.query: Does using a different guest teacher require new confirmation if the workshop keeps its name?

evidence.text: If the named guest is replaced by another artist, a fresh booking confirmation is required even when the workshop title stays the same.

cases.query: Two current guest-workshop documents give different reservation deposits. What amounts do they state?

evidence.text: The office handbook sets the guest-workshop reservation deposit at 35 dollars per participant.
The artist welcome handout sets the guest-workshop reservation deposit at 20 dollars per participant.

cases.query: When can a guest teach without a studio host, and what rule applies if a 15-year-old joins?

evidence.text: Every guest workshop containing any participant under 16 must have a rostered studio host present throughout the teaching period.
For an adult-only guest workshop, the artist may teach without a host in the room after the duty lead signs the adult-session exception.

cases.query: We are replacing the guest rather than moving the same visit. Can we use the free move allowance or do we need a fresh booking?

evidence.text: A confirmed guest workshop may be moved once without an administration fee if the host gives seven full days of notice.
If the named guest is replaced by another artist, a fresh booking confirmation is required even when the workshop title stays the same.

cases.query: A youth workshop is cancelled by the guest: what options do participants receive, and what host requirement would still apply to a replacement youth session?

evidence.text: When a visiting artist cancels, the office offers either a replacement workshop or a full workshop-fee refund within ten business days.
Every guest workshop containing any participant under 16 must have a rostered studio host present throughout the teaching period.

cases.query: After a residency runs in both buildings, which envelope is used for the final host handover sheet?

evidence.text: For a guest residency spanning both buildings, the final host handover sheet must be sealed in the green envelope marked GUEST NORTH.

cases.query: For how many calendar days can a student normally keep a borrowed percussion instrument?

evidence.text: A standard percussion instrument loan lasts 21 calendar days from the signed collection date.

cases.query: How many business days before pickup must a student reserve a loan drum?

evidence.text: An enrolled student must reserve a loan instrument at least three business days before collection.

cases.query: Does a student need to close the loan drum case outdoors on a dry day?

evidence.text: Borrowed percussion must be carried inside its closed case whenever it is outdoors, including in dry weather.

cases.query: How soon must a borrower report a split drumhead or a loose metal part?

evidence.text: A borrower must report a split drumhead or loose metal fitting within 24 hours of discovering it.

cases.query: Can I use disinfectant spray to clean a borrowed practice pad?

evidence.text: Practice-pad surfaces are cleaned with the supplied dry microfiber cloth after each use; students must not spray them with disinfectant.

cases.query: The store and repair bench disagree about the standard hand-drum kit deposit. What are the two current amounts?

evidence.text: The store procedure requires a 45 dollar refundable deposit for a hand-drum kit.
The repair checklist requires a 30 dollar refundable deposit for a hand-drum kit.

cases.query: If a safety recall arrives during my 21-day loan, do I keep the original due date or return it sooner?

evidence.text: A standard percussion instrument loan lasts 21 calendar days from the signed collection date.
A safety-recalled instrument must be returned by the end of the next business day, overriding its ordinary loan due date.

cases.query: May I renew a recalled instrument for the usual extra week? State the ordinary renewal condition and the recall deadline.

evidence.text: A loan can be renewed once for seven days if no other student has reserved that asset.
A safety-recalled instrument must be returned by the end of the next business day, overriding its ordinary loan due date.

cases.query: After a safety recall interrupts my loan, what substitute is offered and what normal loan period anchors the remaining time?

evidence.text: A standard percussion instrument loan lasts 21 calendar days from the signed collection date.
When a safety recall interrupts a current loan, the repair desk offers a practice pad for the remaining original loan period at no additional deposit.

cases.query: For a drum transferred between campuses, what must happen before its student loan time begins?

evidence.text: For an instrument sent between campuses, the receiving clerk must sign the amber transfer card before the loan clock starts.

cases.query: How far before departure is the signed residential consent form due?

evidence.text: A signed residential-tour consent form must reach the tour leader 28 calendar days before departure.

cases.query: What is the main luggage weight limit for the overnight studio trip and is a day bag also allowed?

evidence.text: Each residential-tour participant may bring one main bag weighing at most 12 kilograms plus one small day bag.

cases.query: Can a participant enter a friend's sleeping room on the overnight trip without staff?

evidence.text: Participants may enter only their assigned sleeping room unless a staff lead explicitly accompanies a room visit.

cases.query: How many duty adults must remain awake until the last residential room check is finished?

evidence.text: Residential night cover requires at least two awake duty adults until the final room check is complete.

cases.query: Who must sign in a participant arriving after the residential evening handover?

evidence.text: A participant arriving after the evening handover must be signed in jointly by the tour leader and night-support adult before joining a sleeping room.

cases.query: What conflicting lights-out times are printed in the two current overnight-trip instructions?

evidence.text: The tour leader handbook sets residential-trip lights-out at 21:30.
The night-support notes set residential-trip lights-out at 22:00.

cases.query: Must all medicine be handed over for the trip, or is a rescue inhaler ever allowed to stay with the participant?

evidence.text: All scheduled tour medication must be handed to the designated medicines lead in its original labelled packaging at departure.
A participant may keep a rescue inhaler on their person only when a written self-carry plan is signed by the guardian and medicines lead.

cases.query: A student has a rescue-inhaler self-carry plan. What ordinary medicine rule still applies, and what evening check-in is required?

evidence.text: All scheduled tour medication must be handed to the designated medicines lead in its original labelled packaging at departure.
A participant using a self-carried rescue inhaler must check in with the night-support adult before the evening room check.

cases.query: Can a rescue-inhaler plan justify keeping unrelated scheduled tablets? Explain the normal handover and the narrow permission.

evidence.text: All scheduled tour medication must be handed to the designated medicines lead in its original labelled packaging at departure.
A participant may keep a rescue inhaler on their person only when a written self-carry plan is signed by the guardian and medicines lead.

cases.query: How many business days ahead should a planned sensory adjustment be requested?

evidence.text: A planned sensory adjustment request should reach the support coordinator five business days before the relevant class.

cases.query: When is a new sensory support plan reviewed if a student misses some classes?

evidence.text: An agreed sensory support plan is reviewed after the student's first three attended classes.

cases.query: Can a student ask for a supported break without saying the reason aloud?

evidence.text: A student can show the blue pause card to request a supported break without first explaining the reason aloud.

cases.query: How many students can use the quiet room at once, apart from the adult?

evidence.text: The quiet room may support at most three students at one time, excluding the supervising adult.

cases.query: Which arrival and departure information belongs in the private quiet-room record?

evidence.text: The room lead records a student's arrival and departure times in the private quiet-room log.

cases.query: The sensory guide and room notes give different check-in intervals. What does each current document say?

evidence.text: The sensory planning guide permits a quiet-room break of up to 15 minutes before a teacher check-in.
The room-operation notes require a teacher check-in after ten minutes of an ordinary quiet-room break.

cases.query: May a student keep ear defenders on during class and during an evacuation drill, and what extra condition applies in the drill?

evidence.text: A student may wear their own ear defenders during ordinary class exercises after the teacher confirms a visible stop signal.
During an evacuation drill, a student using ear defenders must have a named adult within sight who can relay the evacuation cue.

cases.query: After using a blue pause card for a quiet break, can a student return alone, or what handover is needed?

evidence.text: A student can show the blue pause card to request a supported break without first explaining the reason aloud.
After a quiet-room break, the student returns with the supervising adult or through a handover directly accepted by the class teacher.

cases.query: What visible support is required for ordinary ear-defender use and what adult support must be in sight during a drill?

evidence.text: A student may wear their own ear defenders during ordinary class exercises after the teacher confirms a visible stop signal.
During an evacuation drill, a student using ear defenders must have a named adult within sight who can relay the evacuation cue.

cases.query: A student requests a break without speaking; who records arrival and departure in the quiet room?

evidence.text: A student can show the blue pause card to request a supported break without first explaining the reason aloud.
The room lead records a student's arrival and departure times in the private quiet-room log.

cases.query: What annual royalty percentage does the studio pay a visiting choreographer for repeating their routine?
What is the studio registration number for international visiting-artist visa sponsorship?
What is the fixed late-return fine per day for a borrowed hand drum?
What exact percentage of a loan drum repair bill is covered by the studio insurer?
What is the residential trip cancellation charge if a family withdraws 11 days before departure?
What dose of travel-sickness medicine should a 12-year-old take on the residential coach?
What is the sensory support coordinator's professional registration number?
Which brand and model of ear defenders will the studio purchase for every sensory support user?
What deposit is required for a visiting artist workshop in June 2029?
How long may I borrow a hand drum in June 2029?

notes: All sources and people are fictional. These 50 questions are a fresh validation set and must not select model or window settings.
All eight sources are simultaneously effective throughout 2027. Conflict questions deliberately require both active documents; no source precedence is supplied.
Evidence is manually authored source text with half-open Unicode character offsets, never chunk IDs or model-derived labels.
Unanswered questions have no supporting answer in the corpus. Returning a nearest neighbour is diagnostic; this experiment does not implement abstention.
Two single-paragraph cross-campus procedures deliberately place required evidence near the tail. No text or label was chosen from reranker output.
Ordinary paragraphs contain similar operational distractors but do not establish unsupported numerical fees, medical doses, clinical eligibility or source precedence.
The data is synthetic and manually authored by the implementation assistant. No external inference API or reranking model was used to create or label it.
